open_points.subject: Cabinet's access to project context
open_points.text: “Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet. ... Each ... reads its context” conflicts with R0-43: “`context` ... answers only a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data` — today PresuPro and Client Portal.”
open_points.question: Does Cabinet receive `context` and therefore a token allowing `personal_data`, or is Cabinet excluded from that operation?
options: Cabinet receives full `context` with `personal_data` authority
Cabinet cannot call `context`
Cabinet receives a separate non-personal projection
open_points.default_guess: Cabinet cannot call `context`; only PresuPro and Client Portal can.

open_points.subject: Migration-source trust boundary
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance ... no production personal data” conflicts with importing the VPS source “with their customers ... objects” into production.
open_points.question: What kind of instance is the legacy VPS migration source, who administers it, and may it contain real personal data before migration?
options: A separately named legacy-production source containing real data
A test instance whose data is synthetic
A test instance allowed to contain pre-production personal data
open_points.default_guess: Treat the VPS source as a separately named legacy-production system administered by the owner and containing real personal data.

open_points.subject: Authentication of test instances
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated” and R0-27 apply to Registry, while “Secrets” names only credentials “in the production instance's configuration.”
open_points.question: Who authenticates to test instances, who owns their credentials, and do the production restrictions on agents and services apply there?
options: Each test instance has independent owner and service credentials
Test instances use a development-only authentication principal
Test instances may waive authentication
open_points.default_guess: Give every test instance independent credentials administered by that instance's human owner, never copied from production.

open_points.subject: External AI provider boundary
open_points.text: R0-68 refers to “the agent's AI provider,” and the exclusions refer to “the external AI providers,” but no actor or trust boundary says which Registry outputs may cross to them or what Registry assumes about them.
open_points.question: Is the AI provider a separate untrusted recipient of every value the agent receives, and which disclosure classes may cross that boundary?
options: Provider receives all agent-visible non-`personal_data` outputs
Provider receives only explicitly designated `open` outputs
Provider handling is entirely outside Registry's guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Model the provider as an external recipient of all agent-visible outputs, permitted to receive `open` and `business_confidential` but never `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: Replay of project, customer and room creation
open_points.text: “A create repeated after a lost answer ... never silently makes a second project, customer or room, and never damages one” does not say what answer or failure the retry produces.
open_points.question: For each replay-safe create, does an equal retry return the original record, fail as a duplicate, or produce another explicit replay result; and what happens when the retried content differs?
options: Return the original record for an equal replay and refuse differing content
Refuse every detected replay without changing state
Return a distinct replay result identifying the original record
open_points.default_guess: Return the original record for an equal replay and refuse a differing replay without changing state.

open_points.subject: Revision checks on non-correction changes
open_points.text: R0-35 says “A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change moves. A change states the revision it was made against,” but the action table requires a revision only for correcting a project or customer.
open_points.question: Which actions must supply and advance a project or customer revision—especially archive, customer erasure, restriction changes, relationship changes, project erasure, and adding a room—and how do stale checks interact with idempotent repeats?
options: Every mutation of the record requires and advances its revision
Only correction operations use revisions
Record mutations use revisions, while child resources such as rooms and pointers do not
open_points.default_guess: Require the current revision for every direct project or customer mutation and advance it on an actual state change; do not move it for unchanged idempotent repeats or independent child records.

open_points.subject: Agent-session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version,” but no action says which changes advance it.
open_points.question: Which events advance the access version: registration, grant, revoke, active-project change or clear, request creation or replacement, request answer, project archive, project erasure, expiry, or session end?
options: Advance for every change to the session access record
Advance only when the granted set or active project changes
Use separate versions for grants, active choice and pending request
open_points.default_guess: Advance one access version for every persisted change to grants, active project, pending request, scope or expiry.

open_points.subject: Repeated session-access transitions
open_points.text: “the project joins the session's granted set,” “the session's active project changes, or is cleared,” and the restriction and relationship actions do not state what happens when the requested state already holds.
open_points.question: What observable result and version behavior apply when granting an already-granted project, selecting the already-active project, clearing an already-empty active project, restricting an already-restricted customer, lifting no restriction, ending an already-ended relationship, or resuming one not ended?
options: Return the unchanged record without advancing a version
Refuse the redundant transition
Accept it and advance the relevant version
open_points.default_guess: Return the unchanged record successfully and do not advance a version.

open_points.subject: Date of relationship ending
open_points.text: “the Customer marked as ended on that date” does not say whether the date is supplied by the owner or generated from the action time.
open_points.question: Is the relationship-end date an owner-supplied effective date, Registry's current date, or a full timestamp generated by Registry?
options: Owner supplies an effective calendar date
Registry records the current calendar date
Registry records its current timestamp
open_points.default_guess: Let the owner supply the effective calendar date and separately keep the normal change timestamp.

open_points.subject: Whole deletion of an archived project
open_points.text: The owner may choose a project “deleted whole,” but only anonymisation explicitly says which linked records survive.
open_points.question: When an archived project is deleted whole, are its rooms and artifact pointers deleted too, and what happens to any internal references to them?
options: Delete the project, object, rooms and pointers atomically
Delete project identity and rooms but retain pointers as detached history
Delete only the project record and leave linked records inaccessible
open_points.default_guess: Delete the entire project aggregate—project, object, rooms and artifact pointers—atomically after removing session grants.

open_points.subject: Audit scope for related records and session state
open_points.text: R0-58 records “changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,” but does not say whether project changes include rooms and artifact pointers or whether registration, active-project changes and pending-request changes are significant.
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries?
options: Only the actions expressly enumerated in R0-58 and R0-66
Every state-changing primary action
Project/customer changes include their rooms and pointers, but ordinary session-request state is excluded
open_points.default_guess: Audit every state-changing primary action except the exclusions explicitly named as ordinary reads, ordinary agent calls and flow internals.

open_points.subject: Failed changes in the audit log
open_points.text: R0-37 says an audit entry records “the outcome,” while R0-58 says Registry records only “significant changes of state.”
open_points.question: Are refused attempts at significant changes logged with their failure outcome, or are only accepted state changes logged?
options: Log both accepted and refused significant mutation attempts
Log only accepted changes, making outcome always successful
Log refused attempts only when they are security-relevant
open_points.default_guess: Log accepted significant changes only; rejected attempts belong to infrastructure security logging unless separately designated.
